symptom: On FactoryManagement 5 of 61 page/snippet XPath rows named a widget (WidgetId/WidgetName) with no row in the widgets table: the MxModelReflection.MxObject and .Token snippets each had one widgets row, table1 (Forms$Table), and nothing inside it. 213 widgets were missing project-wide, and lint rules reading widgets never saw them.
cause: walkWidget descends only into the container keys it names (Widgets, Rows/Columns, Templates, FooterWidgets, TabPages, Object, Items). A Forms$Table keeps its widgets under Cells[]/Widgets, a Forms$ScrollContainer under CenterRegion/Top/Left/Right/Bottom, a Header under Left/RightWidget(s), a SplitPane under First/SecondWidget(s) - none walked. scanXPathUnder recurses into every key, so it found them.
insight: Two walks over the same BSON with different descent rules disagree silently; the XPath rows' WidgetId (#1879) was the first thing to join them, which is what exposed it. To audit coverage, left-join xpath_expressions.WidgetId to widgets.Id per DocumentType - PAGE alone hid it, all 5 misses were SNIPPET rows. Stored key names come from modelsdk/gen/pages init* functions (NewPart/NewPartList), including the CenterRegion storage-name override. A generic walk keyed on isWidgetNode was rejected: it would start indexing named non-widget nodes (Forms$TabPage, grid columns) and change parent ids. Lint diff after the fix on FactoryManagement: one new, genuine MPR012 (a static image inside a page scroll container), nothing removed.
